react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis tools (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-network analysis) converged on two dominant biological themes. The strongest cross-paradigm signal is **galactose metabolism** (KEGG:hsa00052 / SMPDB:SMP00043), which ranked #2 in RaMP (FDR 1.13×10⁻¹²), #0 in MetaboAnalystR (p=5.16×10⁻⁸), and #5 in mummichog (p=0.011). Five driver metabolites drove this hit: sucrose (C00089), myo-inositol (C00137), galactitol (C01697), galactinol (C01235), and glycerol (C00116) — all found in the galactose ↔inositol branch of the Leloir pathway. The second major theme is **glycerophospholipid metabolism**, which emerged independently in RaMP (WP:WP2533, FDR 1.22×10⁻⁵), Reactome (R-HSA-1483206, FDR 5.54×10⁻⁵), and mummichog (rank 2, p=0.0039). The three verified driver metabolites are glycerol (C00116), myo-inositol (C00137), and S-adenosylhomocysteine (C00021), the latter acting as a methyl-group donor that can drive phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis. A lipid-oxidative sub-theme, **arachidonic acid metabolism**, was detected by mummichog (rank 8, p=0.038) through the direct hit of 5,6-EET (C14768), a cytochrome-P450 epoxide of arachidonic acid. L-Cysteine (C00097) and S-adenosylhomocysteine (C00021) together pointed to the **trans-sulfuration pathway** (WP:WP2333, FDR 1.60×10⁻⁴), consistent with methylation-dependent phospholipid remodelling. The convergence of a carbohydrate branch (galactose-inositol) and a lipid-membrane branch (glycerophospholipid/AA) with a shared methyl-donor hub (SAH) suggests the treatment perturbation dysregulates both sugar metabolism and membrane lipid dynamics, possibly through altered methylation capacity.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis tools (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-network analysis) converged on Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:map00052) as the dominant affected pathway across all paradigms. RaMP returned Galactose Metabolism at rank 2 (FDR=1.13×10⁻¹²) with five driver metabolites: myo-inositol, sucrose, galactitol, galactinol, and glycerol. MetaboAnalystR PSEA ranked KEGG:hsa00052 first (p=5.16×10⁻⁸) with an identical five-compound hit set. mummichog's network-activity analysis returned Galactose metabolism at rank 5 (p=0.0137) with twelve overlapping metabolites including D-glucose, sucrose, glycerol, myo-inositol, and galactitol. The convergent signal across ORA and m/z-network paradigms establishes this pathway as the primary biological finding. S-adenosylhomocysteine and L-cysteine together mapped to KEGG:hsa00670 (One carbon pool by folate; p=0.0068) and KEGG:hsa00270 (Cysteine and methionine metabolism; p=0.0108) via MetaboAnalystR, indicating secondary perturbation of one-carbon metabolism. Fumaric acid contributed to no significant single-pathway hit but appeared in the broad Reactome Transport of small molecules (FDR=8.27×10⁻⁶) and ADHD/ASD pathways, suggesting mitochondrial TCA influence independent of the galactose core.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis tools (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-network analysis) converged on two dominant biological themes. The strongest cross-paradigm signal is **galactose metabolism** (KEGG:hsa00052 / SMPDB:SMP00043), which ranked #2 in RaMP (FDR 1.13×10⁻¹²), #0 in MetaboAnalystR (p=5.16×10⁻⁸), and #5 in mummichog (p=0.011). Five driver metabolites drove this hit: sucrose (C00089), myo-inositol (C00137), galactitol (C01697), galactinol (C01235), and glycerol (C00116) — all found in the galactose ↔inositol branch of the Leloir pathway. The second major theme is **glycerophospholipid metabolism**, which emerged independently in RaMP (WP:WP2533, FDR 1.22×10⁻⁵), Reactome (R-HSA-1483206, FDR 5.54×10⁻⁵), and mummichog (rank 2, p=0.0039). The three verified driver metabolites are glycerol (C00116), myo-inositol (C00137), and S-adenosylhomocysteine (C00021), the latter acting as a methyl-group donor that can drive phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis. A lipid-oxidative sub-theme, **arachidonic acid metabolism**, was detected by mummichog (rank 8, p=0.038) through the direct hit of 5,6-EET (C14768), a cytochrome-P450 epoxide of arachidonic acid. L-Cysteine (C00097) and S-adenosylhomocysteine (C00021) together pointed to the **trans-sulfuration pathway** (WP:WP2333, FDR 1.60×10⁻⁴), consistent with methylation-dependent phospholipid remodelling. The convergence of a carbohydrate branch (galactose-inositol) and a lipid-membrane branch (glycerophospholipid/AA) with a shared methyl-donor hub (SAH) suggests the treatment perturbation dysregulates both sugar metabolism and membrane lipid dynamics, possibly through altered methylation capacity.
